raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Under `--scheduling-policy priority`, when a running request cannot get KV blocks the scheduler preempts the lowest-priority running request. `self.running` is in admission order, not priority order, so that request can sit in the middle of the list, for example when higher-priority requests arrived after it. If it is the request currently being scheduled, it preempts itself, and the running loop then `break`s:

```python
if new_blocks is None:
    # Cannot schedule this request.
    break
```

Every running request after it gets no tokens in that step, even though they all have higher priority, the self-preemption just freed blocks, and budget remains. This is a priority inversion: the requests the policy is meant to protect lose a step whenever a lower-priority request ahead of them runs out of KV.

After a self-preemption the request has already been removed from `self.running` (`del self.running[victim_index]` with `victim_index == req_index`), so `req_index` already points at the next request. The fix continues the loop in that case. Nothing changes for FCFS: it preempts `running[-1]`, so a self-preemption there only happens on the last request. Other reasons for a failed allocation (a deferred free that will not help, pending connector frees) still end the loop.

Related but different: #49097 (fixed by #49206) adjusted `req_index` when the victim sits before the cursor. #39375, a larger rework of this preemption path that has been open since March, would also remove this `break`.

## Test Plan

- New `test_priority_self_preemption_keeps_scheduling_later_running_requests`. Setup: one free block, `running = [A(p0), B(p5), C(p0)]`; A and B both need a new block on the same decode step, C does not. A takes the block, B preempts itself, and C must still be scheduled.
- `tests/v1/core` in full, main vs this PR.
- A random-workload stall check on the real `Scheduler` (small per-step budgets, priority/FCFS mixed, hybrid attention+Mamba and full-attention layouts, 40 seeds each). It flags a running request that gets 0 tokens while the step has budget left for its whole remainder; this is how I found it.

## Test Result

(CPU only.)

- New test: fails on main (`{'A': 1}` scheduled, C skipped), passes with this PR.
- `tests/v1/core` in full: same failed/errored set on main `fa75d3456d` and on this PR (68 environment failures on both trees, e.g. missing `torchvision` and offline model configs); 0 failures only on this PR; 953 → 954 passed (the new test).
- Stall check, hybrid layout: main stalls on 1/40 seeds (this bug), this PR on 0/40. Full-attention layout: 0/40 on both, with identical per-run action counts. A KV-content check over 60 more seeds on this PR found nothing.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

AI-assisted (Claude Code). I reviewed the change and ran the tests listed above myself.

files.patch:
@@ -4220,6 +4220,59 @@ def test_priority_scheduling_preemption_victim_selection():
     assert waiting_req_ids == ["1", "0"]
 
 
+def test_priority_self_preemption_keeps_scheduling_later_running_requests():
+    """A running request that preempts itself must not end the running loop.
+
+    Under PRIORITY the preemption victim is the lowest-priority running request,
+    which can sit in the middle of `running`. When it is the request being
+    scheduled, it preempts itself; the requests after it have higher priority
+    and may still fit, so they must be scheduled in the same step.
+    """
+    block_size = 16
+    # One block each for A, B and C, plus exactly one free block.
+    scheduler = create_scheduler_with_priority(
+        num_blocks=5, block_size=block_size, max_num_batched_tokens=256
+    )
+    # A and B (14-token prompts) need a new block on the same decode step; B has
+    # the lowest priority. C arrives one step later, so it sits behind B in
+    # `running`, and never needs a second block here.
+    req_a, req_b = create_requests_with_priority(
+        num_requests=2,
+        priorities=[0, 5],
+        arrival_times=[0.0, 1.0],
+        num_tokens=block_size - 2,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        req_ids=["A", "B"],
+    )
+    (req_c,) = create_requests_with_priority(
+        num_requests=1,
+        priorities=[0],
+        arrival_times=[2.0],
+        num_tokens=10,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        req_ids=["C"],
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(req_a)
+    scheduler.add_request(req_b)
+
+    output = scheduler.schedule()  # prefill A and B
+    _model_output(scheduler, output, [[100], [100]])
+    scheduler.add_request(req_c)
+    output = scheduler.schedule()  # decode A and B, prefill C
+    _model_output(scheduler, output, [[100]] * 3)
+    output = scheduler.schedule()  # decode A, B and C
+    _model_output(scheduler, output, [[100]] * 3)
+    assert [r.request_id for r in scheduler.running] == ["A", "B", "C"]
+    assert scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == 1
+
+    # A and B both cross a block boundary now. A takes the free block, B finds
+    # none and preempts itself; C needs no new block and must still run.
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert output.preempted_req_ids == {"B"}
+    assert output.num_scheduled_tokens == {"A": 1, "C": 1}
+    assert [r.request_id for r in scheduler.running] == ["A", "C"]
+
+
 def test_priority_scheduling_equal_priority_preemption():
     """Test arrival time tiebreaker when requests have equal priority."""
     # This test verifies that arrival time is used as a tiebreaker for equal

@@ -899,6 +899,16 @@ def schedule(self, throttle_prefills: bool = False) -> SchedulerOutput:
                         break
 
             if new_blocks is None:
+                if (
+                    self.policy == SchedulingPolicy.PRIORITY
+                    and request.status == RequestStatus.PREEMPTED
+                ):
+                    # The request was the lowest-priority running request and
+                    # preempted itself. The requests after it have higher
+                    # priority and may still fit (it just freed its blocks);
+                    # it was removed from `self.running`, so `req_index`
+                    # already points at the next one.
+                    continue
                 # Cannot schedule this request.
                 break
